title: Design System: LIHDAY 德運實業

display.purpose: Hero heading only, three hand-broken lines.

statement.purpose: Single words that stand as content: process step names, company values (to 3.5rem).

numeral.purpose: The phone number in the contact section.

title-lg.purpose: Headline sentence inside a scenario panel.

title.purpose: Item names in ruled grids and rails.

lead.purpose: The one muted paragraph beside or under a section heading; max 34em.

body-sm.purpose: Item descriptions, header nav at weight 500, footer.

label.purpose: Terms in fact lists and the footer base line.

button.purpose: Labels of red buttons and the call bar.

shadows.name: floating-call-bar
shadows.purpose: Mobile call bar only; the single element fixed above scrolling content that casts a shadow.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: CSS easing for every state change (--ease-out).

motion.name: expo-out
motion.purpose: GSAP easing for entrances: masked lines, fades, cell fills, digits.

motion.name: expo-in-out
motion.purpose: Iris opening on load and the service grid wipe.

motion.name: back-out
motion.purpose: Small round marks popping in: process dots, the call mark.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Line draws, icon tile fills, tab changes.

motion.name: duration-sheet
motion.purpose: Header hide, mobile menu wipe, call bar slide.

motion.name: line-rise
motion.purpose: Heading lines rising out of their masks.

motion.name: scrub
motion.purpose: Scroll-linked motion: iris stopping down, process rail, values list.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.purpose: Page scroll smoothing; off under reduced motion or ?static.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Brand logo marquee; pauses on hover, static under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
The site is the category-standard security-contractor homepage, built carefully: a white header with a red phone button, a black hero, alternating white, pale-grey and black sections, and one full-red section that holds the phone number. Nothing about the structure is experimental. The character comes from how plainly it is drawn: content sits in grids ruled with 1px hairlines instead of cards, headings are very heavy Traditional Chinese set in two short lines, and red is the only colour that is not black, white or grey.

The one drawn object is a camera lens in SVG. Its iris opens when the page loads, stops down as the hero scrolls away, and its glass drifts against the pointer. Everything else moves in the same grammar: headings rise line by line out of a mask, grids are ruled before their cells fill, the process rail is drawn by the scroll, and the phone number is dialled in digit by digit. Motion eases with expo-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) and settles; the page renders fully still under `prefers-reduced-motion` or `?static`.

Density is moderate and even. Sections breathe at `clamp(72px, 10vw, 144px)`, text columns stop near 34em, and every section ends closer to the phone call than it began.
keyCharacteristics: Three grounds only: ink black, paper white with pale grey, and one full-red contact section.
Hairline-ruled grids and lists carry structure; no bordered or shadowed card containers.
Heavy CJK headings (weight 800 to 900) broken into deliberate lines, each line its own mask.
One radius (4px) for every rectangle; circles only for marks.
The phone number is always the primary action and always red or on red.
A single drawn lens stands in for photography the project does not have.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: `red` is for light grounds and for fills. On ink, red text and red marks use `red-on-dark`. A red-filled button keeps `red` on any ground because its label is white.

rules.name: The One Red Room Rule
rules.body: Red becomes a section ground exactly once, in the contact section. Everywhere else it is a mark: a button, a glyph, a dot, a line, one emphasised word.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: A section is ink, paper (white or `paper-2`), or the red room. No tinted, gradient or image grounds; the hero's ember glow is light from the lens, not a ground.

rules.name: The Written Line Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text is broken into lines by hand in the markup, two for a section and three for the hero. Each line is its own masked block so it can rise on entry. Do not let a heading wrap wherever the viewport decides.

rules.name: The Phrase Break Rule
rules.body: Chinese headings and leads break at phrase boundaries (`word-break: auto-phrase`), paragraphs use `text-wrap: pretty`, headings `balance`.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: 900 for display and statements, 800 for headlines, 700 for titles and actions, 500 for navigation and list facts, 400 for reading. Size alone never separates two levels.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the page flow casts a shadow. A shadow is allowed only on an element that is fixed above scrolling content. Stacking order is fixed: content, call bar (40), header and menu (50), skip link (100).

rules.name: The Lens Is the Only Depth Rule
rules.body: Gradients, bevels, glare and parallax belong to the drawn lens and the ember glow behind it. Interface surfaces stay solid.

dos: **Do** make the phone number the primary action of every surface: a Signal Red button with the phone icon and the digits.
**Do** switch to `red-on-dark` for red text and marks on ink, and keep it to large text and graphics (it measures about 4.3:1 on ink).
**Do** build repeating content as ruled cells: a 1px text-colour rule to open, 1px hairlines between, first column flush with the column edge.
**Do** write section headings as two short lines at weight 800 and wrap each line in its own mask.
**Do** use 4px for every rectangle and full circles only for dots and round marks.
**Do** ease state changes and entrances with `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` or `expo.out`; keep overshoot (`back.out`) for small round marks popping in.
**Do** keep every animated surface complete and readable when motion is off.
**Do** place product photos on `paper-2` plates with multiply blending, and show partner logos as supplied.
donts: **Don't** use red as a section ground outside the contact section.
**Don't** put `red` text or thin red marks on ink; that is what `red-on-dark` is for.
**Don't** wrap content in bordered, shadowed or rounded card containers.
**Don't** add shadows to anything in the page flow.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a second accent colour.
**Don't** use radii between 4px and a full circle, or pill-shaped buttons.
**Don't** use stock scene photography; where there is no real photo, the drawn lens or a ruled grid of facts carries the space.
**Don't** apply gradients, glare or parallax to interface surfaces; they belong to the lens.
